name: Melvins
label: AmRep
lede: Three Montesano high schoolers took their name from a Thriftway supervisor, and Kurt Cobain said watching them made him a punk. Four decades on, the band has outlasted Atlantic Records, put out a record under a mirror-written name and played with two drum kits pushed together.

eras.title: Montesano, and a name from the Thriftway
eras.text: Three classmates at Montesano high school start on Hendrix and The Who covers, swerve into hardcore, then slow everything down. By 1987 Dale Crover is on drums, Kurt Cobain is hanging around rehearsals, and two records are out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Melvins · Wikipedia: Buzz Osborne · Consequence: Three Bastards, 30 Years
years.h: Montesano classmates start a band named for a Thriftway supervisor
years.p: [[Buzz Osborne|9a911b22-f972-44ee-b2d3-d41297fe96e9]], [[Matt Lukin|299e8c0a-63ad-4d49-b492-d3740364da84]] and [[Mike Dillard|a3750a7b-cf02-4e48-b16c-0b61ca820bfa]] begin on Jimi Hendrix and The Who covers, then go fast and hardcore. The name belongs to a supervisor at the Thriftway where Osborne clerked.
years.xp:
Osborne was born in Morton, Washington, and moved to Montesano at 12, per Wikipedia. The early set lists leaned on Hendrix and Cream, and the punk originals came after. All three attended Montesano Jr./Sr. High School.

Wikipedia and a Consequence oral history both date the start to 1983: Osborne on guitar and vocals, Lukin on bass, Dillard on drums. The Thriftway supervisors, Wikipedia says, "felt it to be an appropriately ridiculous name". Consequence has Dillard leaving less than a year in.

years.cap: Flyer for D.O.A. with the Melvins and He-Sluts at the Tropicana in Olympia, September 13, 1984.
years.h: Iron Maiden cover-band drummer Dale Crover replaces Mike Dillard
years.p: Crover becomes the second half of a partnership with Osborne that is still running. Rehearsals move to Aberdeen.

q: When I saw them play, it just blew me away.
years.src: Wikipedia: Buzz Osborne · Wikipedia: Dale Crover
years.h: Kurt Cobain watches the Melvins and walks out a punk
years.p: Cobain, an Aberdeen kid, starts turning up at Melvins rehearsals and shows. That winter he forms Fecal Matter with Dale Crover on bass and Greg Hokanson on drums.
years.xp:
Cobain's full line, per Wikipedia, ends "I was instantly a punk rocker."

Fecal Matter formed in late 1985. After Hokanson left, Cobain and Crover recorded the Illiteracy Will Prevail demo around Easter 1986 at Cobain's aunt's house in Burien, Washington, with Crover on both bass and drums. Wikipedia adds that many of the entries in Cobain's published journals are unfinished letters to Crover.

years.cap: Flyer for Beefeater, RKL and the Melvins at Staches, August 13, 1986.
years.h: Six Songs is recorded at Ironwood Studio and put out by C/Z Records
years.p: The Melvins' first release is a live-in-the-studio session cut on February 8, 1986 in Seattle, pressed as a 7-inch.
years.xp: The session was later expanded into the longer reissues known as 10 Songs and 26 Songs, per Wikipedia and Trouser Press. Lukin played bass on it.

years.h: Gluey Porch Treatments arrives on Alchemy Records
years.p: The first album was recorded in October 1986 at Studio D in Sausalito, California, with Lukin still on bass.
years.xp: Trouser Press, reviewing it later, called it the "sludgiest, heaviest downer music this side of Henryk Góreki".

years.src: Wikipedia: Matt Lukin · Wikipedia: Lori Black
years.h: [[Matt Lukin|299e8c0a-63ad-4d49-b492-d3740364da84]] leaves for Mudhoney; Shirley Temple's daughter takes the bass
years.p: Lukin co-founds Mudhoney with Mark Arm, Steve Turner and Dan Peters. Lori Black joins on bass as Lorax.
years.xp:
Lukin's version, per Wikipedia: Osborne told him he was moving to San Francisco and the Melvins would break up. Lukin found out later that Crover had moved there too and that the band had carried on with Black.

Black was born in 1954, the second child of Shirley Temple, and had played in Clown Alley. Wikipedia's Lori Black article says she was briefly married to Osborne in 1987, and that the bass idea came up while they were dating.

eras.title: San Francisco, and a favor for Nirvana
eras.text: Osborne and Crover move south and the songs get slower and heavier, while the friends they left in Washington get a lot bigger. Crover drums on Nirvana's first demo, and Bullhead sets the template that grunge and doom both borrow from.

years.h: Dale Crover drums on Nirvana's first demo, credited as 'Kurt Kovain'
years.p: On January 23, 1988, Crover plays on Nirvana's ten-song demo at Reciprocal Recording in Seattle, and drums with them live in Tacoma the same day.
years.xp:
Crover ended up on three tracks of Bleach: 'Floyd the Barber', 'Paper Cuts' and 'Downer'. More of the session later appeared on Incesticide and With the Lights Out, per Wikipedia.

He rejoined Nirvana for an August 1990 West Coast tour with Sonic Youth, and drummed on an April 1991 demo of 'Drain You'.

years.h: Osborne is the one who puts Dave Grohl in touch with Nirvana
years.p: After Grohl's Washington, DC band Scream breaks up, Osborne introduces him to Cobain and [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]]. Nirvana's drummer problem is solved a couple of years later.

years.src: Life of the Record · Wikipedia: Melvins
years.h: Osborne quits his job and moves to San Francisco with Crover
years.p: They recruit Lori Black on bass. Osborne says music has paid his way ever since, years before Atlantic.

years.h: Ozma, produced by [[Mark Deutrom|85cf9aef-aa91-4d8a-9340-04b86ed174d6]], comes out on Boner Records
years.p: It is the first recording with Lori Black on bass, credited as Lorax. Deutrom, who produced, joins as bassist a few years later.
years.xp: Trouser Press described it as an "outpouring of overweight weirdness cut into short slices".

years.cap: Buzz Osborne on guitar at the Cattle Club, Sacramento.
years.h: Japan's Boris takes its name from a Bullhead song
years.p: Boner's second Melvins album stretches the songs and drops the tempo, the drone-sludge template that followed.
years.xp:
Trouser Press called it the "clearest exposition of Melvin-hood to that point, and the blueprint for much of what was to follow". Boris named themselves after the song 'Boris', per Wikipedia.

Boner also put out the Eggnog EP the same year, built around a 20-minute experimental piece.

eras.title: A major label, and a producer fired midway
eras.text: The Melvins lose an album title to a cleaning-product maker, then sign with Atlantic at Kurt Cobain's suggestion. Cobain starts Houdini in the control room and does not finish it, and the era ends with a noise record under a backwards name.

years.h: Boner gives Osborne, Crover and Joe Preston a solo EP each
years.p: King Buzzo, Dale Crover and Joe Preston are a nod to Kiss's four solo albums of 1978. Preston has replaced Black on bass.
years.xp: Preston plays on the 1992 Salad of a Thousand Delights and on the album released under the name Melvins, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The album called Lysol is renamed Melvins
years.p: A trademark problem sends Boner and Tupelo to the tape and ink. Joe Preston plays bass on the self-titled result.
years.xp:
Boner learned after pressing that Lysol was a registered trademark of Lehn & Fink. Per Wikipedia, a company representative posed as a magazine interviewer to gather information. Boner covered the word with black tape and ink, and early copies could be peeled clean. Later ones were damaged in the attempt.

The 31-minute record is six tracks run as one piece, with covers of Flipper's 'Sacrifice' and two Alice Cooper songs. AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it "the logical extension of the sheer monstrosity of the band's work".

years.cap: The Melvins on stage at Soma, March 1993, six months before Houdini came out.
years.src: Wikipedia: Houdini · Life of the Record · Wikipedia: Melvins
years.h: Cobain's suggestion lands the Melvins at Atlantic with Houdini
years.p: Atlantic president Danny Goldberg signs the band at Kurt Cobain's suggestion, with creative control. The album is cut in roughly two weeks.
years.xp:
The sessions were split across Brilliant Studios and Razor's Edge in San Francisco and the Laundry Room in Seattle. 'Honey Bucket' was released on August 30 and got MTV airplay. The album also has a cover of Kiss's 'Goin' Blind'.

Osborne told Life of the Record that the album sold over 100,000 copies, and that he never expected Atlantic to keep the band beyond one record. He was also surprised the label never interfered with what they recorded. It entered Billboard's Heatseekers chart at No. 29.

years.big: I couldn't make it work with him.
q: I had no interest in going public with Kurt's problems.
years.src: Louder · Life of the Record · Wikipedia: Houdini
years.h: Osborne asks Atlantic to take Cobain off the Houdini sessions
years.p: Cobain, brought in to co-produce, is missing from sessions. Garth Richardson takes over, and Cobain keeps his credit and plays guitar on 'Sky Pup'.
years.xp:
Osborne told Metal Hammer in 2021, as reported by Louder: "During the last part of him being there, he was a mess, drug-wise." Life of the Record says Cobain was dealing with heroin addiction and often did not show up. Atlantic's Goldberg had put the exit down to scheduling.

Osborne also says Cobain played percussion on 'Spread Eagle Beagle'. Engineer Jonathan Burnside recalled "bad communication, drugs, major label profiteering, rehab, schedule blowouts".

years.h: Mark Deutrom, who produced Ozma, takes over the bass
years.p: Lori Black, credited on Houdini though Osborne disputes how much she played, is gone by spring. Deutrom stays through 1998.

years.h: "Complete and utter nonsense," Osborne says of Prick
years.p: The Melvins still owe Atlantic, so the noise record goes to [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s Amphetamine Reptile under the mirror-written name ƧИIV⅃ƎM, released August 5, 1994.
years.xp:
It was recorded in April 1994 and first meant to be called Kurt Kobain. The band changed the title after Cobain's death that month so it would not read as a tribute, per Wikipedia.

Osborne's own description: "a total noise crap record we did strictly for the weirdness factor." Trouser Press listed the contents as "newsreel interviews, acoustic and demi-electric jams...ambient noise, church bells and anything else left lying around".

years.cap: Osborne singing at the Cattle Club, Sacramento.
years.src: Life of the Record · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Melvins
years.h: Osborne ranks Stoner Witch above Houdini
years.p: He calls Houdini "not a high point", and fans tend to name Stoner Witch as the Atlantic record to start with.
years.xp: Critics were split. Trouser Press found a transitional record that lacked "the special everything that makes the Melvins unique", despite plenty of rock force.

eras.title: Atlantic lets go, AmRep picks up
eras.text: Sitar, trombone, a 25-minute silence and a night in Melbourne. After three albums Atlantic drops the band, and the next records come out on Amphetamine Reptile.

years.h: A sitar and a trombone turn up on Stag
years.p: The third and last Atlantic record, on a Mammoth/Atlantic imprint, reaches No. 33 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp: Trouser Press said it "brings back the spunk" after Stoner Witch, with unexpected instruments and acoustic blues on the way.

years.cap: Buzz Osborne singing at Garage D'or Records in Minneapolis, July 5, 1997.
years.src: Wikipedia: Melvins · Life of the Record
years.h: Atlantic lets the Melvins go after three albums
years.p: The band had expected to be dropped after one. Osborne says the label never interfered with what they recorded.

years.h: Honky ends on 25 minutes of silence, unless you buy the vinyl
years.p: Recorded February 12 to 17, 1997 and released May 5 on Amphetamine Reptile, with Deutrom on bass.
years.xp:
The last track runs about four minutes of music, then more than 25 minutes of silence. Without it the album drops from 70:53 to 45:43. The vinyl leaves the silence off and splits 'Air Breather Deep in the Arms of Morphius' in two.

The Melvins and Joe Barresi produced it. Kat Bjelland sings on it, Mac Mann plays keyboards and David Scott Stone plays bowed cymbal and oscillators. Reviews were mixed: NME gave it 1/10.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alive at the Fucker Club
years.h: Alive at the F*cker Club is cut opening for Cosmic Psychos
years.p: Recorded August 23, 1997 at the Corner Hotel in Richmond, Melbourne, and released by AmRep in 1998. It runs about 21 minutes.
years.xp:
The band played three consecutive nights, August 22 to 24, as support to Cosmic Psychos. The trio is Osborne, Crover and Deutrom.

It opens with 'Boris' and carries an uncredited jam on Deep Purple's 'Smoke on the Water'.

years.h: Kevin Rutmanis of The Cows takes the bass for seven years
years.p: Deutrom exits. Osborne also joins [[Fantômas|057aa66c-cf6e-499d-bda8-5adc47ad4197]] with [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]] this year.

eras.title: Ipecac moves in and the band spreads out
eras.text: Mike Patton's Ipecac Recordings becomes the home label and starts reissuing the back catalog. Along the way come a trilogy, a drone collaboration with Lustmord, a deli-meat photo on Tool's website and a bassist who leaves.

years.h: Mike Patton's Ipecac Recordings signs the Melvins
years.p: The label starts remastering the back catalog and puts out The Maggot, The Bootlicker and The Crybaby across 1999 and 2000, some with guest vocalists.

years.h: A Melvins message to Tool, spelled in lunch meat
years.p: On a 2002 Australian tour, the band photographs the words "Melvins say... Tool Sux!" in deli meat, and the picture ends up on Tool's own website.

years.cap: The Melvins on stage at Roskilde Festival in Denmark.
years.h: Lustmord joins for Pigs of the Roman Empire
years.p: A slow, heavy collaboration with ambient artist Lustmord, released on Ipecac.

years.h: Kevin Rutmanis leaves in June, after a cancelled European tour
years.p: A European tour planned for October 2004 is cancelled amid unexplained complications with Rutmanis. He returns briefly in early 2005 and officially leaves in June.

eras.title: Two drummers, then 51 nights
eras.text: Big Business's Jared Warren and Coady Willis join and the band plays as a quartet with fused drum kits. Then a Melvins Lite line-up plays every state in 51 nights.

years.cap: The Melvins on stage, October 13, 2006: Osborne, Crover and the Big Business pair.
years.h: Big Business joins, and the Melvins fuse two drum kits
years.p: [[Jared Warren|0bc59e8e-4911-4f0f-b851-3a638af30235]] and [[Coady Willis|3e4cad92-f9bf-4a70-8d9e-188aec7d87f2]] come in after the band's Los Angeles move, first appearing on (A) Senile Animal. Crover and Willis set their kits up as mirror images.
years.xp:
Willis described the plan as a "mirror image" arrangement, per Wikipedia: "We've kind of fused our two drum sets together, and we're going to try and do some crazy thing with it."

Big Business, the bass-and-drums duo Warren and Willis founded in Seattle in 2004, kept going alongside.

years.h: Two nights at Great American Music Hall for Jello Biafra's 50th
years.p: Osborne, Mike Dillard on drums and Crover on bass play two San Francisco shows in June, performing only The Mangled Demos.

years.cap: Dale Crover behind the kit at Slim's, San Francisco.
years.h: Melvins Lite plays all 50 states and D.C. in 51 nights
years.p: Osborne, Crover and [[Trevor Dunn|0dee6bef-335d-4f29-92b2-4d84b0e48552]] open in Anchorage on September 5 and finish in Honolulu on October 25, a record for consecutive states, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: The tour began the same week as Freak Puke, the Lite record. A tour film, Across the USA in 51 Days: The Movie!, followed.

eras.title: The 1983 line-up returns, then the bass chair rotates
eras.text: For the 30th anniversary the original drummer comes back and Crover moves to bass. Bassists come and go until Steven McDonald of Redd Kross settles in, and the Melvins keep putting out records.

years.cap: The Colossus of Destiny: A Melvins Tale, a feature documentary filmed around the 30th anniversary.
years.src: Consequence: Three Bastards, 30 Years · Wikipedia: Melvins
yt: The Colossus of Destiny: A Melvins Tale
years.h: Mike Dillard returns for Tres Cabrones, thirty years on
years.p: Founding drummer Dillard rejoins Osborne for the 30th anniversary, with Crover moving to bass. Ipecac releases the album on November 5.
years.xp: The album is billed as the closest thing to the original Melvins, per the Consequence oral history. The 1983 line-up recorded again on Working with God (2021) and Thunderball (2025).

years.h: Butthole Surfers' Paul Leary and Jeff Pinkus join for Hold It In
years.p: Osborne and Crover team up with the two Butthole Surfers on a record out in October 2014.

years.cap: Osborne, Crover and McDonald on stage in Edmonton.
years.h: Steven McDonald of Redd Kross takes the bass chair
years.p: Warren and Willis of Big Business leave, and McDonald joins the Melvins as bassist. He is still there.

years.h: Five bassists share Basses Loaded, Krist Novoselic among them
years.p: McDonald, Novoselic of Nirvana, Trevor Dunn, Jared Warren and Jeff Pinkus take turns, with a different bassist on almost every track.

years.cap: The Melvins at the Bijou Theater, Knoxville.
years.h: Spinal surgery sidelines Dale Crover, and Coady Willis steps back in
years.p: Willis fills in on the 2023 US tour while Crover recovers. In 2025 the Melvins co-headline with Napalm Death and release Savage Imperial Death March on February 16.
years.xp: That spring 2025 tour was the first since 2016 with both Crover and Willis on drums. Tarantula Heart came out April 19, 2024 as the 27th studio album, and Thunderball, with the 1983 line-up, followed on April 18, 2025.
